title: VONKO-033: Characteristics, treatment patterns and survival among adults with renal carcinoma, with a particular focus on subgroups of patients with (a) renal cell carcinoma and (b) early-stage renal cell carcinoma receiving adjuvant therapy – a study based on cancer registry data
summary:
Kidney cancer can develop in different parts of the kidney, but the most common type is called renal cell carcinoma, which accounts for about 95% of all cases. In Germany, around 14,000 to 15,000 people are diagnosed with kidney cancer each year. Men are affected much more often than women, and the disease usually occurs in older adults. The chances of recovery depend greatly on the stage at which the cancer is detected: if it is found early, the outlook is relatively good, but it becomes much worse in advanced stages or if the cancer returns. About one third of cases are detected early, often by chance during imaging tests such as ultrasound or MRI that are performed for other reasons.

The main form of treatment is usually surgery, in which part or all of the affected kidney is removed. However, in some patients the cancer comes back later, especially if certain risk factors are present. In recent years, treatment options have improved significantly. For example, a large study showed that a medication called pembrolizumab, given after surgery, can reduce the risk of the cancer returning and improve survival. For more advanced stages of the disease, modern treatments are now available, including immunotherapy and targeted drugs, which are often used in combination.

Because treatment in everyday medical practice is not always the same, it is important to collect real-world data. This helps researchers understand which treatments are actually being used and how well they work. Such information is essential for improving patient care and supporting better decisions in healthcare.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of kidney, except renal pelvis

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of patients with renal carcinoma diagnosed between 2014 and 2026 in Germany

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients 
1. with newly diagnosed renal carcinoma (ICD-10 C64) diagnosed in 2014 or later
2. aged 18 or over
3. residing in the relevant federal state at the time of diagnosis
4. with at least one day of survival / follow-up period
Exclusion criteria:
1. The case is known to the register solely on the basis of
a. a death certificate (DCO case) 
b. a pathology report 
c. a follow-up report 
d. a report to the tumour board 
e. a combination of the aforementioned report types 
2. Unknown vital status at the end of the follow-up period
